title: In collaboration with the WCS and ArtW, Anita Glesta's Brooklyn Bridge video projection highlights the Hudson Canyon
summary: In collaboration with the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) and ArtW , and presented through the New York City Department of Transportation’s art program (NYC DOT Art), internationally recognized multimedia artist Anita Glesta , will premiere AQUA COSMOS: The Hudson Canyon, a monumental eighteen-minute immersive projection that will transform the Brooklyn Bridge into a gateway to one of the world's most extraordinary marine environments. Observers can see the public art installation projected on the Brooklyn Bridge from the Emily Warren Roebling Plaza, Brooklyn Bridge Park, September 25 and 26, 7pm to 10 pm each evening. The Hudson Canyon, located 100 miles off the coast of New York City, is the largest submarine canyon along the Atlantic Coast. title: Christie's Geneva presents Exceptional Jewels & Objects of Elegance: A Connoisseur's Collection
summary: Christie's presents Exceptional Jewels & Objects of Elegance: a Connoisseur's Collection, an unparalleled private collection comprising nearly 300 twentieth century jewels, magnificent Art Deco vanity cases and fine 18th and 19th century gold boxes, all of which epitomise the timeless elegance and enduring appeal sought by today's connoisseurs. Assembled over four decades with a collector's eye and a curator's sensibility, the Collection reflects an unwavering commitment to excellence, guided by a profound understanding of style, rarity and craftsmanship. The discerning owner pursued only the finest gemstones and most exceptional creations, acquiring masterpieces from some of the world's most revered jewellers, including Van Cleef & Arpels, Graff, Bulgari and David Morris, among others. Expected to realise in excess of US$25 million, this remarkable Collection ranks among the most important to appear at auction in recent years, distinguished not only by the calibre of its content but a

title: Native American artistry and creatures from deep time share the spotlight at Artemis auction
summary: A monumental California basket woven with patterns recalling the markings of a rattlesnake, an ancestral Puebloan bird vessel, a rare Mississippian portrait pot and the fossilized remains of creatures that inhabited the Earth millions of years before humans are among the highlights of Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo’s September 15 auction. Bringing Native American material into dialogue with fossils, meteorites and other natural-history specimens, the sale creates an unusual journey through time — from objects shaped by Indigenous hands and traditions to evidence of animals and cosmic events that predate human history altogether. The auction forms the first half of a two-day collaboration between Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo . Day 1 focuses on Pre-Columbian and Native Americ

title: Almine Rech Brussels presents Hans Op de Beeck solo exhibition Vanishing Point
summary: Almine Rech Brussels is presenting 'Vanishing Point,' Hans Op de Beeck’s first solo exhibition with the gallery, on view from September 10 to November 7, 2026. In a world saturated with images, speed, and constant distraction, the work of Hans Op de Beeck offers something that today seems almost radical: silence. His installations, sculptures, films, and drawings do not loudly demand attention; rather, they slowly draw the viewer into meticulously constructed universes where time appears suspended and meaning unfolds gradually. To look at an Op de Beeck work is less to observe a work of art than to enter a mental space where memory, desire, and imagination converge. His pieces seem frozen in a precise instant; objects remain abandoned yet intact, while narratives hover somewhere just beyond reach. His art does not explain—it suggests. title: Rotterdam warehouse to be transformed into Europe's largest dance production center
summary: Detailed designs by the internationally acclaimed Chinese architects, MAD, were revealed today for the new Danshuis in Rotterdam. Situated on a landmark site in the historic dock area of Rotterdam, adjacent to the recently opened Fenix museum of migration, also designed by Ma Yansong/MAD, the new Danshuis is planned to open in 2030. Danshuis will be the largest centre for the production and development of dance of all styles under one roof in Europe, open to all ages and levels of experience, and providing the best facilities for the creation of professional and amateur dance programmes. The designs will transform the 9,500 square metres art deco building, a former warehouse dating from 1923 on the south bank of the River Maas in central Rotterdam. title: David Zwirner presents Thomas Ruff exhibition of 9/11 photographs in New York
summary: David Zwirner is presenting an important group of photographs by Thomas Ruff at the gallery’s 533 West 19th Street location in New York. Featuring images from jpegs ny, a subset of the artist’s larger jpegs series, the twelve works on view are derived from images of the World Trade Center attacks in New York on September 11, 2001. Coinciding with the twenty-fifth anniversary of the attacks, this exhibition was conceived by the artist as a commemoration of that day. Prior to the exhibition in New York, this group of works was also on view as part of Unlimited at Art Basel 2026. Ruff was in New York on September 11, 2001, and he shot numerous photographs documenting that day and its aftermath, but when he returned home to Germany several days later he realized there were no images on his camera. Three years later, in 2004, the event was still front of mind for the artist. Seeking an appropriate artistic response to tragedy on such an unimaginable

title: Norman Lewis survey at Michael Rosenfeld Gallery explores the influence of music
summary: Michael Rosenfeld Gallery is presenting Norman Lewis: Jumping Jive, the gallery’s seventh solo exhibition dedicated to the work of Norman Lewis (1909–1979). Featuring paintings and drawings representative of Lewis’ over four-decade career, the exhibition highlights the vital role music—from jazz and blues to classical, pop, and reggae—played in the artist’s life and practice. An important thematic and conceptual throughline in Lewis’ oeuvre, music appears in early figurative depictions of bands and jazz clubs, in later abstract compositions that variously recall music notes or pulsing soundwaves, and in titular references to songs, lyrics, or musical icons. As Lewis increasingly embraced abstraction in the mid-1940s, the intuitive, riff-based method of jazz composition guided his approach to painting. This focused survey of Lewis’ diverse body of work not only evidences the inspiration the artist gleaned from music but also reveals how his unders

title: F-117 Nighthawk joins the National Air and Space Museum Collection
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum is welcoming a Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk stealth fighter, the world’s first true operational stealth combat aircraft, into the national collection. This remarkable aircraft will be transferred to the museum by the U.S. Air Force. It was prepared for its public display by the team at Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works, and the U.S. Air Force Reserve’s 512th Airlift Wing will transport the F-117 from the Skunk Works’ facility to Dulles International Airport in Virginia aboard a C-5 Galaxy cargo plane. The Nighthawk will be displayed at the museum’s Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center in Chantilly, Virginia, in late October. This donation was announced today at the Air & Space Forces Association's Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland. title: Daniel Jorge debuts new soapstone sculptures and installations at Mendes Wood DM
summary: Mendes Wood DM is presenting Cantaria, Daniel Jorge’s first solo exhibition in São Paulo. Held in the Barra Funda warehouse, the exhibition brings together previously unseen works, including sculptures, wall reliefs, installations, and performance, and is accompanied by an essay by the curator and researcher Carlos Quijon Jr. The exhibition’s title refers to the craft of the stonemason – the technical expertise of stone carving – which the artist has mastered. The word also evokes a song, as in the ritualistic and labor-related sounds that accompany the carver. It is from this intersection of hand and voice, precision and improvisation, that Jorge’s practice takes shape. In his works, the material does not arrive on its own, but is accompanied by the labor, the exchanges, and the stories that brought it there. title: Kandinsky returns to Rome after 25 years in major Palazzo Bonaparte retrospective
summary: More than twenty-five years after Rome last hosted a major exhibition devoted to Vassily Kandinsky, the Russian-born pioneer of abstraction is returning to the Italian capital in a sweeping retrospective at Palazzo Bonaparte. Opening September 15, 2026 and continuing through February 14, 2027, the exhibition brings together more than seventy works from international museums and the Centre Pompidou in Paris, whose Kandinsky holdings are among the most important in the world. Produced and organized by Arthemisia in collaboration with the Centre Pompidou and curated by Angela Lampe, curator of the modern collections at the Musée national d’art moderne, the exhibition follows Kandinsky’s development from his early figurative work to the radical experiments that helped reshape modern painting. title: Sean Kelly presents Anthony McCall solo exhibition Solid Light, 1973, 2020, 2026
summary: Sean Kelly is presenting Solid Light, 1973, 2020, 2026, Anthony McCall’s seventh solo exhibition with the gallery. Bringing together three significant works spanning over fifty years of the artist’s career, the exhibition traces the remarkable evolution of McCall’s pioneering solid light works, from his groundbreaking Line Describing a Cone, 1973 to Skylight, 2020 and the debut of his newest work Swarm, 2026. The exhibition reveals the sustained rigor with which McCall has redefined the possibilities of sculpture, drawing, cinema, and sound, to create groundbreaking immersive environments. Anthony McCall is widely regarded as one of the most influential artists working with light and moving image. Emerging from the avant-garde film communities in London and New York during the late 1960s and early 1970s, he rejected the conventions of narrative cinema in favor of an investigation into the essential properties of film

title: Peter Beard's monumental Kenya Tusker leads Heritage's wide-ranging photographs auction
summary: More than a century of photographic innovation comes into focus Oct. 1-2 in Heritage’s Photographs Signature® Auction, an expansive sale of more than 600 lots by over 200 photographers. Ranging from early modernism and landmark photojournalism to fashion, celebrity portraiture and monumental contemporary work, the auction offers both museum-caliber rarities and accessible opportunities for collectors. Leading the auction is Peter Beard’s Kenya Tusker, for The End of the Game, June 1960, an extensively inscribed mixed-media work on canvas. The largest print of this celebrated image to appear at auction, it combines Beard’s imposing portrait of an elephant with handwritten observations drawing a provocative parallel between the survival crises facing elephants and humans as expanding populations compete for finite land and resources. “Few auctions demonstrate the extraordinary breadth of photography

title: Roy Lichtenstein and Andy Warhol lead Christie's London prints sale
summary: Christie's will present Prints & Multiples, an online sale and exhibition in London this September Prints season, celebrating editions from established artists and emerging talents from the early 20th century to the present day. Roy Lichtenstein's seminal Two Nudes from the artist's Nude Series, his final major body of work, is one of the lead highlights of the season. Numbered 18 in an exclusive print run of 40, the work is estimated to reach £150,000-200,000. Andy Warhol's monumental, glittering Mickey Mouse, from Myths (1981, estimate: £150,000-200,000) is a further highlight of the sale. Covered with diamond dust, Mickey Mouse is one of Warhol's most iconic images. From the edition of 200, this work evokes Warhol's characteristic playfulness and is a favourite from the Myths series. Other rare works include Banksy's iconic Flower Thrower Triptych (Grey) from 2019 (estimate: £100,000-150,000), coming to auction as one of only a few examples issued from the studio in the original art

title: Christie's to auction photography collection of interior designer Vicente Wolf
summary: Christie's will offer The Vicente Wolf Photography Collection—the personal collection of renowned interior designer Vicente Wolf this October in New York in a two-part single-owner sale—one live and one online. The offerings include nearly 200 exceptional photographs, lovingly assembled by the famed designer over the course of nearly half a century. Vicente Wolf, internationally celebrated figure in the world of interior design, is best known for his impressive eye and range as a creative visionary across residential, hospitality and commercial spaces. While building a successful business and name for himself in the design world, he simultaneously refined his eye as a prolific and passionate collector of photography, originating with advice given to him by Richard Avedon. title: Andy Warhol retrospective brings Pop Art, personal memories and rare documents to Rome
summary: Andy Warhol’s unmistakable images of celebrities, consumer goods and popular culture are at the center of a major retrospective now open at La Vaccheria in Rome, where the exhibition Andy Warhol – Forever Love brings together artworks, photographs, documents and personal memories to explore both the public icon and the man behind one of the twentieth century’s most influential artistic identities. On view through March 28, 2027, the exhibition features 51 works by Warhol, more than 60 documents concerning his life and career, and 37 works by other major Pop artists associated with his cultural world. Curated by Gianfranco Rosini, it combines familiar Warhol imagery with more intimate material intended to place the artist within the network of friendships, encounters and experiences that shaped his life. title: Art Gallery of Ontario debuts new acquisitions by Toronto artist Brian Groombridge
summary: This fall at the Art Gallery of Ontario, Toronto artist Brian Groombridge (b. 1953) opened a solo exhibition of prints and sculptures from 1989-2021. Brian Groombridge: New Models for Measurement is curated by the AGO’s Associate Curator of Canadian Art, Renée van der Avoird and features six new acquisitions, alongside loans from the artist's studio and a private collection. Born in Sarnia, Ontario, Groombridge has applied a poetic, philosophical approach to human knowledge systems since he started his artistic practice in the 1970s. Inspired by cosmology, geography and art history, he often references tools from graphic design, carpentry, and surveying in his prints, sculptures and installation works. Featuring 12 works made between 1989-2021, New Models for Measurement is Groombridge’s first-ever solo exhibition at the AGO. The works

title: Tada Minami retrospective at Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo highlights 70 years of innovation
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo is presenting a major solo exhibition of Tada Minami (1924–2014), a leading abstract artist whose work spans sculpture, design, and architecture in postwar Japan. Tada, who produced approximately 200 sculptural pieces and 500 works integrated into architectural spaces over the course of her career, extended her practice far beyond the confines of the museum, leaving her creations in a wide range of urban spaces—including parks, railway stations, city halls, hotels, and theaters—where they have formed an integral part of people’s everyday life over many years. title: Bergen Kunsthall presents its autumn 2026 program
summary: For more than two decades, Sung Hwan Kim (b. 1975, Seoul; lives and works in Honolulu) has developed a distinctive artistic practice that intertwines video, music, storytelling, performance, drawing, sculpture, and architecture. The exhibition at Bergen Kunsthall builds upon "Protected by Roof and Right-Hand Muscles," the largest European survey of Kim's work to date. The exhibition was first shown at the Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, and was originally curated by Yolande Zola Zoli van der Heide. Original concept by Sung Hwan Kim. The exhibition is developed in partnership with Framer Framed, Amsterdam, the Netherlands and ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe, Germany. title: Man Ray retrospective in Parma brings together more than 300 works across photography, painting, film and design
summary: Man Ray spent his life resisting the idea that an artist should belong to a single medium. He photographed what he did not want to paint, painted what could not be photographed, turned ordinary objects into unsettling sculptures, made experimental films and continually revisited his own inventions. That restless approach to art is at the heart of Man Ray: Everything, opening September 12 at the Villa dei Capolavori, home of the Fondazione Magnani-Rocca near Parma. Bringing together more than 300 photographs, paintings, sculptures, objects, graphic works, books and films, the exhibition is described as the most comprehensive retrospective ever devoted to Man Ray in Italy. title: Christie's celebrates 60 years of Wines & Spirits, opening with The Cellar of the Hon. Henry Tang
summary: Opening the celebrations of Christie’s Wines and Spirits Department’s 60th Anniversary this year, Christie’s presents The Cellar of the Hon. Henry Tang, a dedicated live auction taking place on 10 October 2026 at Christie’s Asia Pacific headquarters at The Henderson in Hong Kong. This landmark single-owner auction comes nearly six decades after Christie’s held its inaugural wine auction on 11 October 1966 in London, a pioneering moment that helped shape the modern fine wine auction market and laid the foundations for the world’s first standalone wine department. Six decades on, Christie’s continues to connect collectors across continents and generations, with the private collection of the Honourable Mr Henry Tang leading the anniversary celebrations in Hong Kong, with further anniversary sales in New York and London to be announced.

title: Fortes D'Aloia & Gabriel presents Tadáskía solo exhibition espírito jardim humana
summary: Fortes D’Aloia & Gabriel presents espírito jardim humana, Tadáskía’s first solo exhibition with the gallery. The exhibition brings together a new body of work. Grounded in memory and imagination, the works contribute to the construction of the artist’s cosmology, in which abstract forms, organic elements, and recurring figures give shape to a cast of nonhuman characters. In paintings on canvas and works made on sculptural supports in leather paper, the artist develops a vocabulary of forms that evokes a universe inhabited by presences, lending a kind of animism to abstract forms, as though beings associated with the animal and vegetal worlds—among them insects, butterflies, and serpents—were taking shape within them. Branches, twigs, fruits, liquids, and other sculptural forms extend this vocabulary into space, where what is suggested in the paintings

title: kaufmann repetto presents Clarissa Tossin solo exhibition Piante Vagabonde
summary: kaufmann repetto presents Piante Vagabonde (Wandering Plants), the first solo exhibition with the gallery by Brazilian artist Clarissa Tossin, bringing together a new body of recent works. Through painting, sculpture, installation, and video, Tossin develops a practice that intertwines ecology, colonial history, and the exploitation of natural resources, examining the relationship between the body, the landscape, and socioeconomic infrastructures. Her work is grounded in the idea that nature is not a realm separate from human experience, but rather a network of relationships of which we are an integral part—one shaped by material and political histories that continue to inform the present. In recent years, her work has been presented at major international institutions, including the recent survey exhibition Point of No Return at the Museu de Arte

title: Hill Art Foundation announces fall exhibition Thucydides Fever Dream curated by Xin Wang
summary: The Hill Art Foundation announced its exhibition for the fall of 2026, "Thucydides Fever Dream." Curated by the writer and art historian Xin Wang, the show situates the rich landscape of contemporary Chinese art in textured relationships to art history, geopolitics, and technology. The exhibition positions emerging names from China's avant garde alongside major works from the Hill Collection and from private collections and institutions around the world.
